skill.name: creating-hooks
skill.description: Guides users through creating Claude Code hooks for automation, validation, context injection, and workflow customization.
skill.summary: Create, configure, test, and harden Claude Code hooks with event references and Bash templates.
skill.author: BrendanShields

security_audit.summary: The static findings are primarily Markdown examples, visible Bash hook templates, local configuration paths, and protective sensitive-file patterns. I found no prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration, hidden installation, or unauthorized network behavior in the scanned files. Users should still review adapted hook scripts before enabling them because hooks can affect tool execution.

remediation.issue: Template scripts can become executable hooks after users copy them into a project.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note that templates should be reviewed, narrowed to a project, and tested before enabling them.

remediation.issue: The context injector forwards project state into model context.
remediation.suggestion: Document that values loaded from project files should come from trusted sources or be sanitized before injection.

remediation.issue: The guide documents a user-level Claude Code settings path.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend project-local settings by default and warn that user settings can affect every project.

static_findings.snippet: # Use jq to ensure valid JSON

| `UserPromptSubmit` | User sends message | Inject context, validate |
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | Load context, init state |
| `Stop` | Agent finishes | Decide if should continue |

content.value_statement: Claude Code hook behavior can be hard to configure safely from memory. This skill guides event selection, settings configuration, script templates, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code hook events and when to use each one.
Provides settings structures for command-based hook configuration.
Includes Bash templates for basic hooks, context injection, and file protection.
Shows how to parse hook input and return decision output.
Documents matcher patterns, exit codes, timeouts, and manual testing.
Describes safety practices such as quoting variables and blocking path traversal.
limitations: Requires users to adapt shell scripts for their project and environment.
Assumes Claude Code hook semantics and Bash-compatible scripts.
Does not replace security review for custom hook commands.

use_cases.title: Create Project Hook Automation
use_cases.description: Developers can choose events and build hooks that log, validate, or shape tool behavior.

use_cases.title: Protect Sensitive Files
use_cases.description: Security teams can adapt the file protector template to block edits to secrets and key files.

use_cases.title: Add Session Context
use_cases.description: Tooling maintainers can inject project metadata at session start to keep coding agents aligned.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a simple Claude Code hook. Ask which event I need, then provide a safe setup plan and test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Tool Matcher
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hook configuration for Claude Code that runs only before Write and Edit actions. Explain the matcher choice and timeout.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Protection Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PreToolUse file protection hook for my project. It should block secret files, reject path traversal, and explain each rule.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Hook Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Claude Code hook workflow with SessionStart context, PreToolUse validation, and PostToolUse checks. Include testing and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Create a hook that blocks edits to environment files.
output: Recommended event: PreToolUse with a matcher for write and edit tools.
Suggested behavior: reject path traversal and block protected filename patterns.
Testing guidance: run the hook with safe and blocked file paths before enabling it.

output_examples.input: Add project context when a Claude Code session starts.
output: Suggested behavior: read trusted project metadata and return concise context.
Safety note: avoid injecting secrets or untrusted instructions into the session.

output_examples.input: My hook is not firing for edit operations.
output_examples.output: The skill would check the hook event, matcher pattern, settings location, script path, executable command, and manual test output.

best_practices: Start with the narrowest event and matcher that satisfies the workflow.
Quote variables, validate hook input, and reject path traversal before file operations.
Test hooks manually with sample input before adding them to project settings.
anti_patterns: Using a global hook when a project hook is sufficient.
Allowing hook scripts to run broad shell commands without input validation.
Logging sensitive file paths or secret names without retention rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you create Claude Code hooks that run on events such as tool use, session start, and prompt submission.

faq.question: Does it install hooks for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that you review, customize, and install yourself.

faq.question: Which hook events are covered?
faq.answer: It covers PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, and related events.

faq.question: Can I use it to protect secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a file protection template that blocks common secret, environment, certificate, and key file patterns.

faq.question: What tools does it assume?
faq.answer: The templates assume Claude Code hooks, Bash scripts, local project paths, and jq for JSON parsing.

faq.question: Is custom hook code automatically safe?
faq.answer: No. Review every custom command, validate inputs, and prefer project-local settings before enabling a hook.
